historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.6% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 4.6% (>30% apart): FY2020-25 EPS was depressed by cloud-transformation double-running costs, breach-related charges and acquisition amortisation while equity compounded through retained earnings; revenue 5yr CAGR 8.0% sits close to the equity figure and is the better organic anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less award-tax withholding): FY2020 $454.3M, FY2022 $36.1M, FY2025 $1,040.9M. The 3-year figures (owner 206%, reported 104%) are arithmetically correct but meaningless: FY2022 was the trough of the cloud build (capex $624.5M, 12.2% of revenue) with a $200M working-capital outflow. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR of 18.0% exceeds the reported 16.7% because SBC grew slower than cash flow (SBC 1.7% of revenue in FY2020, 1.5% in FY2025); SBC is not eating the growth here. Owner FCF 5yr CAGR is flattered by the capex normalisation and should not be extrapolated; the growth paths below are revenue-led.

scenario_narratives.base: Mortgage stays near its ~50%-depressed level through FY2027 and only partially normalises from FY2028; growth is carried by non-mortgage Workforce Solutions (Talent, Consumer Lending, Government -- ~$300M of new ACV benefiting 2027+), USIS non-mortgage and Latin America (Boa Vista, Circulo de Credito). With the ~$3B EFX Cloud build complete, capex settles at the 6-7% framework and margin recovers ~2.5pp over five years from cloud decommissioning and the $150M AI cost target. Buybacks at ~$0.9-1.1B/yr hold the count flat. Terminal cap of 18x owner FCF binds below the Gordon value.
scenario_narratives.bull: A rate cycle turn restores mortgage origination toward historic volumes in FY2028-29; because The Work Number and USIS mortgage revenue carry ~50%+ incremental margins the recovery compounds into both the top line (double-digit growth for three years) and a pre-SBC EBITDA margin of 35.5%, above the FY2021 peak. Verification exclusivity holds against Argyle/Truework, TWN Income and AI-embedded products (54 launched in H1 2026) lift price per transaction, and Latin America scales. 20x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mortgage rates stay near 7% for years, hiring remains at ~50k/month, and verification challengers plus payroll-data aggregators erode The Work Number's pricing, so growth after the guidance year settles at 3-4.5% with no operating leverage: pre-SBC EBITDA margin stuck at 30% (GAAP ~28.5%). A CFPB/state privacy regime adds compliance cost, capex stays at 7%+, and leverage from the bolt-on programme (net debt/EBITDA ~2.8x) limits buybacks. 15x terminal cap and 2.5% terminal growth reflect a business the market would then price as a mature cyclical rather than a compounder.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Equifax is a data oligopoly whose value is a growing owner-FCF stream: The Work Number's exclusive employer feeds and the credit-bureau triopoly are hard-to-replicate assets, but roughly a third of revenue is a call on U.S. mortgage and hiring volumes that are currently at a trough. The valuation charges SBC and withholding in full, holds the count flat (funded by buybacks), builds margin and capex from components rather than carrying the FY2025 FCF forward, and caps the terminal at 15-20x owner FCF so the answer does not rest on the exit multiple. With the price near its 52-week low and ~17x forward adjusted EPS, the finding is whether the market's cyclical pessimism is over-discounting a structural franchise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mortgage-rate path: USIS and Workforce Solutions mortgage revenue carry the highest incremental margins; a higher-for-longer outcome keeps the bear path live
Verification competition (Argyle, Truework, payroll-API aggregators) undercutting The Work Number pricing or exclusivity
Regulatory: CFPB/state credit-reporting and privacy rules constraining data use; 2017 breach obligations run to Jan-2029
M&A cash is outside the flows: a large acquisition (beyond Circulo de Credito) would add debt not modelled here
Terminal value is a large share of EV at an 8.5% WACC; the required-return table shows how fast value falls with the discount rate

data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 33185) via EFX_Metrics.csv and kpis (FY2007-Q2 2026); diluted share count, interest expense, debt split, cash taxes, acquisition cash and withholding taxes read directly from the companyfacts API on 2026-09-28
data_sources.qualitative: EFX_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Q2 2026 results and guidance, segment commentary, bull/bear cases

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 117.48M basic on the 10-Q cover (2026-07-10) plus the 0.8M dilutive effect shown in the Q2 2026 EPS table (119.2M diluted vs 118.4M basic weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the buyback programme (FY2025 $927.5M, H1 2026 $560M) is what funds the flat count in practice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $78.4M plus $15.0M taxes paid on net-share settlement (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). Equifax publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $927.5M; H1 2026 $560M. Active repurchaser: the flat share count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (Friday); valuation run Monday 2026-09-28 pre-open

acquisitions_cash.note: Bolt-on M&A cash is NOT deducted from the flows; Circulo de Credito (Mexico) is pending. Growth paths are treated as organic-plus-small-bolt-on; a large acquisition would need its own bridge item.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.1% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~9.9%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (3.7% after 24% tax) on $5.47B debt; market cap $17.5B -> ~77/23 E/D -> WACC 8.5%. Held identical across scenarios; risk is charged once, in the driver paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside opex, hence inside EBITDA, so the lease charge is already in the flows; operating lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (one treatment, never both). No separate lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial (<1% of net income); flows are treated as fully attributable, no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (owner-FCF margin still ramping in year 5 as capex normalises from the cloud build and EBITDA margin recovers). Routed via dcf-methods: Equifax is a US operating company (data/analytics oligopoly), so the standard owner-FCF route applies and the non-US/cyclical adaptations file was not needed (USD filer, leases in opex, no NCI, no excluded income). EBITDA margin paths are stated PRE-SBC (GAAP EBITDA + SBC + award-tax withholding) so that the engine's SBC deduction returns the GAAP figure less the withholding cash. FY2025 anchors: GAAP EBITDA $1,822.1M (30.0%), + $93.4M SBC-incl-withholding = 31.5% pre-SBC; D&A $726.9M (12.0%, ~a third is acquired-intangible amortisation which fades unless replaced by M&A); capex $481.4M (7.9%, down from the FY2022 cloud-build peak of 12.2%); cash taxes $197.7M on $894.9M pretax (22%), or ~23% on an unlevered basis once the interest tax shield (~$51M) is added back. Interest income is zero: Equifax is net-debt, so nothing to strip. Working capital: deferred revenue is flat (~$100-135M for a decade), so wc_capture is 0. Y1 = FY2026 is discounted a full year although 9 months have elapsed, which is the folder convention and mildly conservative. Cross-check on FY2025: component build gives unlevered owner FCF ~$1,145M vs reported-FCF-less-SBC $1,041M (levered, after ~$160M after-tax interest) -- consistent within a working-capital swing.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the $6.71-6.78B guidance midpoint (+11.0% reported, ~10% constant-currency organic). FY2027 steps down to 7% as the mortgage trough persists and the H1-2026 comparison is tough, offset by ~$300M of government ACV signed in H1 2026 and Circulo de Credito; FY2028 7.5% assumes a partial mortgage normalisation; thereafter decays 0.5pp/yr toward 4%, consistent with Equifax's stated 7-10% organic framework only in its early years.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 31.0% in FY2026 (H1-2026 GAAP 29.2% + 1.5pp SBC/withholding, mortgage mix drag) recovering 0.5pp/yr to 33.5% by FY2031 as cloud double-running costs end and the $150M AI cost target lands; 33.5% pre-SBC equals ~32% GAAP, still below the FY2021 peak of 33.1% GAAP.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex glides 7.5% -> 6.5% (management's post-cloud framework is 6-7%). D&A glides 12.0% -> 9.0% as acquired-intangible amortisation from Boa Vista/Kount/Appriss rolls off; D&A enters only via the tax shield, so the decline is the conservative direction.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax 23% (FY2025 cash tax 22% of levered pretax; adding back the ~$51M interest shield gives ~23%) ramping to 24% as amortisation deductions fade; GAAP rate is 25.8%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 20%: the guidance year has already disappointed (FY2026 revenue midpoint ~$6.75B vs prior Street ~$7.39B, shares -8% on the Q2 print), the two demand drivers that matter (mortgage and hiring) are both weak at once, and net debt/EBITDA sits near 2.8x after the M&A run. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs a rate-driven mortgage recovery, which management does not control, though it needs only that one thing. No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear stays well below a distressed weighting.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
